newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Rybkin in Chechnya for talks on economy.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Rybkin in Chechnya for talks on economy.

text.p: The secretary of Russia's policy-making Security Council, Ivan Rybkin, flew to the Chechen capital Grozny on Sunday to resume talks with separatist leaders over relations between Moscow and the breakaway region.
Itar-Tass news agency said the discussions would focus on economic and monetary issues. Deputy prime minister Movladi Udugov is expected to head the Chechen delegation.

Economic reconstruction is a top priority for Chechnya's newly elected president Aslan Maskhadov following a fierce two-year war between pro-independence guerrillas and Russian troops that ended with last August's peace agreement.
Much of the tiny, oil-rich territory is in ruins and Chechnya desperately needs Russian money to help rebuild its shattered infrastructure.

Despite holding internationally-approved elections in January, Chechnya's political status remains unclear. The peace deal deferred a final decision for five years but Maskhadov and his government insist their region is already independent.

Another major concern for Maskhadov is restoring the rule of law in Chechnya. Two days ago he issued a decree ordering the death sentence or life imprisonment for convicted kidnappers following a rash of abductions by lawless bands.
But there was still no word on Sunday about the fate of Italian press photographer Mauro Galligani, seized by four armed and masked men a week ago outside Grozny.
Italy's ambassador to Moscow, Emanuele Scammacca, has said his government is ready to negotiate with the kidnappers but has ruled out paying a ransom.
